summary: A stone tower on a submerged Lake Superior reef, 24 miles from shore, lit in 1882 and long called the lighthouse farthest from land in the United States.

access.note: Not open to the public; on open water 24+ miles from shore, reachable only by boat in a suitable weather window.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Record lists both 1882 and 1883 for the tower. Sources: foundation pier finished August 1880, tower courses laid 1881, lit 4 July 1882, protection pier removal completed September 1883. Putnam gives 1877-1882; the 1924 Bulletin says the tower was built in 1880.

notes_for_editor: Primary Lighthouse Board reports for 1866-1883 are not in the local corpus; construction chronology rests on LighthouseFriends (secondary) plus Johnson 1889, Putnam 1917 and two 1882 newspaper items. The 1866 Board wording is quoted via LighthouseFriends. The 1904 stranding of Chambers and his men rests on LighthouseFriends alone. NRHP nomination PDF is not digitised. Sources disagree on whether the light is still active (USLHS: no; GLEN: Coast Guard maintains it as an active aid); automation 1961/62 unresolved; Light List not checked. 1961 explosion hour differs (night per caption/LF; USCG 2015 article says morning). Distance from shore varies (24, 27.5, 28 statute miles; Marquette 40-45). Johnson 1889 OCR reads '101 J feet' (taken as about 101 feet). NY Tribune 1882 page OCR is badly garbled; the 4 July reading rests on one garbled line. January 1922 Bulletin item OCR is corrupt; page matched via the 1918-23 index (pp. 209-210), year 1921 from LighthouseFriends and issue date. Bulletin 1929 radiotelephone item (July 28) read as 1928 from the issue date (2 Jan 1929). Keeper names/years are the USLHS roster as printed; Pasque and Armbruster other-station links come from LighthouseFriends. 'Mackinac Island' for Chambers is the Sun feature's wording. Position correction not proposed: record has two positions >500 m apart (OSM 47.1832,-87.2253; USLHS 47.1828,-87.2253 is within 50 m, Wikipedia 47.18350,-87.22512); no source here shows a real error.
